profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and computing company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Its website for the Nemotron product line describes the company as building multimodal foundation models intended for agentic AI applications, with a stated focus on open-source accessibility, enterprise deployment, and support across hardware platforms including NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. The site describes NVIDIA as working with partners including model builders and AI-native companies, citing ServiceNow as one collaborator involved in evaluating visual question-and-answer accuracy.

NVIDIA's tracked AI products include Nemotron, described as a family of multimodal, open models designed for long-running agents handling tasks such as reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation, speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation. The site highlights Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as a variant aimed at faster task completion, and NeMo Switchyard as a routing component. The company also tracks NVIDIA NIM, a set of inference microservices for deploying foundation models in enterprise environments with GPU optimization and self-hosted options. Nemotron models are published under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which the company describes as permissive and requiring no attribution, while enterprise deployment via NIM requires an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license. Bryan Catanzaro, identified as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site discussing the Nemotron vision.

NVIDIA's SEC profile carries CIK 0001045810 and trades under the ticker NVDA. Its most recently recorded annual revenue figure, from a 10-K filing with a period ending January 25, 2026, was $215,938,000,000. The held facts note 181 legal exposure entries associated with California but list no specific active cases.
